CXMT.why: China's largest DRAM maker (DDR5, LPDDR5/5X, LPDDR6 and DDR5 server modules); its revenue moves with the AI-driven DRAM shortage and prices
CXMT.evidence: CXMT 2026 half-year report: China's No. 1 and the world's No. 4 DRAM maker by shipments and sales; H1 2026 revenue +873.64% as the global DRAM shortage lifted prices and volumes

players.product: DDR5 (up to 8000Mbps), LPDDR4X, LPDDR5/5X and LPDDR6 DRAM chips, DDR5 RDIMM / MRDIMM / UDIMM / SODIMM and LPCAMM modules, and DRAM wafers

quarterly_data.signal: H1 2026 revenue rose 873.64% YoY; the company attributes the jump to fast-growing global compute demand and major makers' capacity reallocation, which left DRAM in short supply with sharply rising prices, lifting both DRAM prices and sales volumes. Main-business gross margin was 84.84% at period end.

H1 2026 revenue by product and channel: LPDDR series slightly above DDR series; most sales go through distributors (buy-out distribution) rather than direct sales. DRAM chips were the main product shipped and sold.

Supply: the global DRAM shortage continued in H1 2026 with prices still rising; CXMT's capacity utilisation stayed high, and its capacity scale ranks first in China and fourth globally (it is China's No. 1 and the world's No. 4 DRAM maker by shipments and sales). Management expects the global DRAM supply shortage to continue in H2 2026; it is negotiating long-term supply agreements with several leading customers to lock in mid- to long-term demand.

Technology and products: 1st- to 4th-generation process platforms are in mass production and the 5th-generation platform was in customer certification at the report date. DDR5 (16Gb/24Gb/32Gb, up to 8000Mbps) and LPDDR4X / LPDDR5/5X (up to 10667Mbps) are in volume production, automotive-grade LPDDR4X and LPDDR5X are in mass production, and LPDDR6 (peak 12800Mbps, up to 16GB per chip) has been sampled to key customers with mass production being accelerated. DDR5 modules include server RDIMM and MRDIMM.
quarterly_data.figure: LPDDR6 peak 12800Mbps, 16GB; LPDDR5/5X up to 10667Mbps; DDR5 up to 8000Mbps

quarterly_data.signal: Customers: CXMT names Alibaba Cloud, ByteDance, Tencent, Lenovo, Xiaomi, Transsion, Honor, OPPO and vivo as core end customers; LPDDR4X is in the supply chains of Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo, Transsion and Lenovo, and LPDDR5/5X in those of Xiaomi and Transsion. Customer concentration is relatively high because end demand is concentrated and sales go through a small number of distributors.

Management view on AI: AI-driven DRAM demand and major makers' capacity reallocation were among the main reasons for H1 growth, but CXMT's revenue share from AI-related fields was relatively low in the period; it says continued sharp price increases are not sustainable and that international makers' planned capacity additions could reverse the supply-demand balance if demand lags. On 8 June 2026 (US time) the US Department of Defense added its subsidiary CXMT Memory to the Section 1260H Chinese military companies list; the company says this will not materially affect operations.

Investment and R&D: total R&D investment rose 87.38% (part of it capitalised as projects met capitalisation criteria); fixed assets were 38.79% of total assets and depreciation rose 27.85% as capacity construction continues; 7,491 R&D staff (33.42% of employees).
quarterly_data.figure: R&D investment RMB 6,859,484,480.64 (+87.38%), capitalised RMB 1,322,048,660.04; fixed assets RMB 1,815.63 hundred-million; depreciation RMB 145.10 hundred-million (+27.85%)
